implementation: The ordinary option grammar is isolated in parser/commands/options.rs. Each field uses the existing handlers and validators. On a failed whole-deck pass, a token cursor restores the field start and its scalar/vector/schedule boundary is consumed without evaluation or numeric placeholders, allowing later fields to select physical temperatures.

Option failures share the existing first-error retention with parameter declarations, including physical included-source attribution. A later assignment cannot erase the error; the fresh immutable-source parser must validate every field before returning a netlist. Cancellation and resource errors remain terminal, and standalone materialized option overlays remain fail-fast and atomic.

OUTPUT/RESTART positional look-ahead no longer evaluates expressions or consumes statistical samples. It recognizes authored expression/signed operands syntactically, then the ordinary numeric reader performs validation and sampling.
The existing TEMP/TNOM replay bound, scalar-versus-sweep TEMP precedence, physical overrides and scoped temperature binding remain in use.
acceptance_evidence: Two baseline public regressions failed at eager RELTOL and TEMP division-by-zero operands before later same-card TEMP/TNOM assignments were discovered. Both now return the exact expected option values.

Fifteen public option regressions cover same-card assignments, implicit numeric values, numerical validators, package transitions, pending parent temperatures in nested scopes, time vectors, OUTPUT and RESTART positional schedules, scalar/sweep precedence and inactive literal hints.

Independent seeded expression contexts verify one draw per schedule operand, a following eager declaration and the next unused draw for OUTPUT and RESTART, and verify exact eager option sample order through a failed temperature pass.

Stable invalid options, duplicate overwrites and incomplete values remain errors. Included continued option errors retain options.inc:2. Later option vector resource exhaustion retains ParseError::ResourceLimit, and materialized option overlays preserve their input on failure.

The private cancellation test visits every abort poll across failed schedule discovery and successful replay, asserting no polls after abort. Existing parameter/source/model/analysis and CLI temperature/control/origin regressions remain active.
limits: A retained temperature-option group can still stop at a provisional failure before binding later independent TEMP/TNOM entries. The failed committed-source CLI reproduction below is explicitly outside delivered eager-field recovery.

Other eager parameter error classes, unresolved conditional/subcircuit-header decisions, general statistical/runtime binding, inner-loop cancellation and allocation/performance evidence remain open. No C00-C14 package closes.

Earlier Rust 1.94/1.95 compiler and native WASM-runner reliability incidents remain C14 work. CLI runtime qualification continues to use Rust 1.95; successful runs here do not establish general toolchain reproducibility.
